title: A Basic Introduction to the Trace & Trajectory Framework—The Mimetic Stratum (Version 10.0)
content: The Trace & Trajectory Framework (TTF) offers a non-representationalist approach to meaning, cognition, and selfhood grounded in dynamical systems theory and radical enactivism. Rather than treating meaning as stored in mental representations, TTF proposes that meaning is enacted through temporally extended navigational patterns (trajectories) traversing dynamic structures called ribbons. A layered ontology comprises traces (probabilistic preconditions), threads (filamentary configurations emerging as the first semiotic coherence structure over trace sets), ribbons (coordinated thread-bundles with fold dynamics), and trajectories (meaning-events). The stack from threads upward is grounded in semiotic coherence (SC)—an architectural property, not a force or mechanism. A parameter triad—$\lambda$ (structural granularity), $\varsigma$ (semiotic depth), $\sigma$ (epistemic access mode)—governs navigation across these levels. Navigational space exhibits toroidal topology ($\mathbb{T}^2_{\mathcal{H}}$): the Gaussian saturation profile is a cross-section of an asymmetric torus whose upper half carries the saturative convergence gradient and whose lower half maps the dissolutive gradient toward NET substrate. Autosimilar collapse ($\mathcal{A}$) is a navigational-epistemic function, not a structural property. A three-factor convergence model (architectural predisposition 0.55, mimetic fold dynamics 0.30, emergent navigation 0.15) replaces single-factor accounts. The skein ($\mathrm{Sk}$) formalizes how trajectories at different tick rates compose into navigational regimes, dissolving inscriptional accounts of duration and memory through frame coherence trajectoriality (FCT). Three Structural Principles (SP-1 Onto-epistemic Openness, SP-2 Generalized Isomorphy, SP-3 Phenomenal Equivalence) govern the relation between analytical apparatus and phenomenal experience. The Mimetic Stratum ($Msrt$) situates the transductive stratification (T-1, T-2, T-3), while depth mimesis ($Mdepth$) resolves the $\varsigma$/$\sigma$ parametric knockout. The analytical apparatus—Hx namespace, QRS-CONFIG, stratified epistemic barriers, hex bands, and Macro-$\alpha$—jointly handles phenomena typically addressed through separate domain-specific machinery. The framework dissolves rather than solves classical problems—including symbol grounding, the scalability challenge, and the tension between embodied and abstract cognition—by rejecting the representationalist premises that generate them.
